title: Reversing, Signallers & Plant Safety
whatItIs: Reversing is a major cause of deaths on site: HSG144 says about a third of fatal construction transport accidents. Plant also kills by striking people and overturning.

keyFacts.text: Where a vehicle could endanger people, they MUST be warned, by the driver or the person directing it.

keyFacts: Only trained, authorised signallers should direct vehicles.
Signallers stand in a safe place, never directly behind a reversing vehicle.
Driver can't see the signaller? Stop at once until contact is back.
Keep out of the slewing area of excavators: the driver is watching the boom.
Wear the seat belt on plant, even when roll-over protection (ROPS) is fitted.

visual.caption: Controlling reversing: most effective first (HSG144 Table 3)

items.title: Remove or reduce reversing
items.text: One-way systems, turning areas, fewer vehicle movements.

items.title: Keep people out
items.text: Marked reversing areas, no pedestrians, physical stops.

items.title: Safe system of work
items.text: CCTV, mirrors, sensors; signaller in constant contact.

items.title: Warnings
items.text: Alarms and lights: the lowest level of protection.

a.label: Signaller (banksman)
points: Sees the driver and is seen

b.label: Driver
points: Uses vision aids or a signaller
Stops if the signaller is out of sight

onTheTest.question: You are guiding a reversing lorry and step out of the driver's view. What should the driver do?
options: Carry on slowly using the mirrors
Sound the horn and keep reversing
Stop until driver and signaller can see each other
onTheTest.why: HSG150 para 303: drivers who can't see the signaller should stop immediately. HSG144 Table 5: if not visible to each other, stop the vehicle.

onTheTest.question: What is the most effective way to cut the risk from reversing vehicles on site?
options: Remove the need to reverse, e.g. a one-way system
onTheTest.why: HSG144 para 39, INDG199: the most effective way is to avoid reversing, with one-way systems and turning areas.

traps: A reversing alarm alone is not enough: warnings are the last line of protection.
Telehandlers can have a big blind spot at the front right with the boom raised.
Over 60% of dumper deaths involve overturning: keep to safe gradients.
Slewing plant needs over 0.5 m clearance from obstructions, or fence the area.
